_comment: Hand-maintained half of the credits. scripts/build_attribution.sh joins this to what
demscore.countries says is actually drawn and writes webapp/config/attribution.json,
which is what the app reads. Nothing here is derived, and nothing derived is here.
Every geometry_source_dataset present in demscore.countries (or in the historical
registry) must appear in `sourceCredits` below, or the build fails. That is the same
shape as check_country_resolution.sh failing on an unmapped country: a boundary source
that reaches the map without reaching the credits is a licence breach, so it is a build
error rather than a silent omission.
_sourceCreditsComment: One entry per geometry_source_dataset as demscore.countries spells it. `credit` names
the work being credited, so the four CShapes variants collapse into two blocks in the
dialog while the data table can still label a row with the exact table its polygon came

natural_earth.title: Natural Earth 50m
natural_earth.citation: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data at naturalearthdata.com.
natural_earth.role: Present-day country identity, the hexagon geometry every current country is drawn from, and the land basemap.
natural_earth.modifications: Sovereigns dissolved from their map units, overseas units removed, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh.

cshapes_2.0.title: CShapes 2.0
cshapes_2.0.citation: Schvitz, Guy, Seraina Rüegger, Luc Girardin, Lars-Erik Cederman, Nils Weidmann, and Kristian Skrede Gleditsch. 2022. “Mapping the International System, 1886-2019: The CShapes 2.0 Dataset.” Journal of Conflict Resolution 66(1): 144-161.
cshapes_2.0.role: Period-aware historical country boundaries from 1886, and the present-day outlines of Palestine and Zanzibar, which Natural Earth does not carry as separate countries.
cshapes_2.0.modifications: Selected per country-period, some periods extended or merged to cover a coding unit's own span, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh.

cshapes_europe.title: CShapes-Europe
cshapes_europe.citation: Cederman, Lars-Erik, Luc Girardin, Carl Müller-Crepon, and Yannick Pengl. 2025. Nationalism and the Transformation of the State: Border Change and Political Violence in the Modern World. Cambridge University Press.
cshapes_europe.role: Period-aware European boundaries from 1816, including the pre-unification German and Italian states.
cshapes_europe.modifications: Selected per country-period, some periods extended backwards to cover a coding unit's own span, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh.

historical_basemaps.title: Historical Basemaps
historical_basemaps.role: World snapshots for 1783, 1800 and 1815, used only for the entities and years neither CShapes series reaches.
historical_basemaps.modifications: One snapshot year's polygon carried across a span of years, reprojected to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and cut into a hexagon mesh. Every polygon taken from a snapshot is graded low confidence for this reason.

demscore_custom.title: Demscore project approximation
demscore_custom.role: A low-confidence marker near Aden so V-Dem's pre-1967 South Yemen values are drawn somewhere honest rather than across the later People's Democratic Republic.
demscore_custom.modifications: Drawn by hand, reprojected and cut into a hexagon mesh like every other polygon.

_mapOutputComment: The ShareAlike consequence. The hex meshes and the rendered tiles are adaptations of
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 material, so they can only be offered onward under the same terms.
Stated here rather than derived because it is a project decision, not a measurement --

mapOutput.statement: The hexagon meshes and the map tiles rendered from them are adaptations of CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 boundary data, so they are offered onward under the same licence: attribution, non-commercial use, and share-alike. This deployment is itself non-commercial — no advertising, no paid access and no bundling into a commercial service.
mapOutput.note: A view can mix GPL-3.0 and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 polygons in one image; at 1830, for instance, the map draws both. The image is treated as a mixed-source map: each source stays credited above, and the GPL-3.0 notice travels here.
